note: Let s=sin x cos x. 3(1-2s)^2 = 3-12s+12s^2; 6(1+2s)=6+12s; 4(1-3s^2)=4-12s^2. Sum = 13, all s-terms cancel. Verified numerically at x = 0.3, 1.1, 2.7, -0.8, 5.0 (all give exactly 13.0), so the constant is confirmed at points where sin/cos differ in sign and magnitude.
25+20=45, so (tan25+tan20)/(1-tan25 tan20)=1, giving tan25+tan20 = 1 - tan25 tan20, hence the sum is 1. Numerically 1.0000000.
tan t + cot t = 2/sin 2t; 2t = 135 deg, sin 135 = 1/sqrt(2), so value = 2 sqrt(2). Numerically tan 67.5 + cot 67.5 = 2.82842712474619, identical to 2 sqrt(2) to 40 digits.

Componendo-dividendo: (sin(x+y)+sin(x-y))/(sin(x+y)-sin(x-y)) = 2 sin x cos y/(2 cos x sin y) = tan x/tan y, and the RHS becomes 2a/2b = a/b. Verified by solving the given relation numerically for x with y = 0.4 fixed, at three DISCRIMINATING (a,b) pairs where a/b differs from b/a: (5,2) -> 2.5, (7,3) -> 2.3333, (2,9) -> 0.22222. Each matches a/b, none matches b/a.

Product cos(2^k t), k=0..3, equals sin(16t)/(16 sin t) with t = pi/15; sin(16 pi/15) = sin(pi + pi/15) = -sin(pi/15), so the product is -1/16. The sign is the whole point (cos(8pi/15) < 0). Numerically -0.0625 exactly.

The expression equals tan(3x-2x) = tan x wherever it is defined, so it would need tan x = 1, i.e. x = n*pi + pi/4. But at every one of those x, 2x = 2n*pi + pi/2, so tan 2x is undefined (cos 2x = 0 checked for n = -2..3) and the expression itself is undefined. Sympy returns nan at x = pi/4 while the LIMIT there is 1 - that limit is the trap. A scan of 200000 points on (-6,6) found NO x with value within 1e-6 of 1. FLAG: option C is defective independently of this, since it omits n = 0 and all negative n, so it is not the full formal solution set either.

cot x + cosec x = (1+cos x)/sin x = cot(x/2) = sqrt(3), so x/2 = pi/6 and the principal value is x = pi/3; x - pi/6 = pi/6. Root-solved numerically: x = 1.0471975512 = pi/3, check cot x + cosec x = 1.7320508076 = sqrt(3). A sign-change scan on (-2pi, 2pi) found only x = pi/3 and pi/3 - 2pi, confirming x = 2n*pi + pi/3. Option A (pi/3) is the value of x itself, not of x - pi/6.

5-12-13 with b = 13 opposite B, so cos B = (25+144-169)/(2*5*12) = 0 exactly and B = 90 deg. tan(B/4) = tan 22.5 = sqrt(2) - 1 = 0.41421356237, matching option D to 40 digits (sqrt(2)+1 = 2.414, sqrt(3)-1 = 0.732, sqrt(3)+1 = 2.732 all excluded).
Each arccos lies in [0, pi], so a sum of 3pi forces all three to equal pi, i.e. x = y = z = -1. Then xy + yz + zx = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. Checked 3*acos(-1) = 9.42477796 = 3pi.

(sin t - 1)/cos t = -tan(pi/4 - t/2), so arctan gives t/2 - pi/4 = 1 - pi/4 at t = 2, and that value 0.2146 lies inside (-pi/2, pi/2) so the principal branch is correct. Direct computation: arctan((sin 2 - 1)/cos 2) = 0.21460183660255169, equal to 1 - pi/4 to 40 digits. Note sin 2 - 1 and cos 2 are BOTH negative, so the quotient is positive - option D is the sign trap.

A.P. gives 2b = a + c, so ax + 2by + c = a(x+y) + c(y+1) = 0 for all admissible a, c, forcing x + y = 0 and y + 1 = 0, i.e. (1, -1). Tested all four options against five distinct A.P.s (1,2,3), (5,7,9), (-2,1,4), (3,3,3), (0,5,10): only (1,-1) satisfies every one.

a = r/p (y = 0) and b = -r/q (x = 0, since -qb = r), so a + b = r/p - r/q = r(q-p)/(pq). Sympy: option B minus (a+b) simplifies to 0; options A and C do not. Discriminating numeric p=2, q=3, r=6: a+b = 3 - 2 = 1, and B = 1, C = -1, A = 5, D = -30. The sign of b is the whole question.

The two lines meet at (4/3, 4/3). With A = (2h, 0), B = (0, 2k) the midpoint is (h, k), and the line x/(2h) + y/(2k) = 1 through (4/3, 4/3) gives (2/3)(1/h + 1/k) = 1, i.e. 2(h+k) = 3hk. Verified at four DISCRIMINATING slopes m = -1, -2, -0.5, -3: 2(h+k)-3hk = 0 in every case, while the other three option-expressions are non-zero and slope-dependent (m = -1 gives the symmetric point h = k = 4/3, so the other slopes are what separate the options).

x = 5 and y = 3 are perpendicular and meet at (5,3), so the bisectors are y - 3 = +/-(x - 5). Joint equation (y-3)^2 - (x-5)^2 = 0, i.e. x^2 - y^2 - 10x + 6y + 16 = 0; sympy confirms option B minus this expands to 0. Spot check (6,4), a point on y-3 = x-5: 36 - 16 - 60 + 24 + 16 = 0. Option A is the ORIGINAL pair of lines, not the bisectors; option D factors as (x-3)(y-5), a different pair.

xy = 0 is the pair x = 0, y = 0, so the triangle has vertices (0,0), (1,0), (0,1) with the right angle at the origin; the orthocentre of a right triangle is the right-angle vertex. Confirmed by solving two altitude equations simultaneously in sympy: {xo: 0, yo: 0}.
